t.7.25.1: Having given that dreadful forest to Khara and having consoled his sister, Daśagrīva became delighted and more at ease.
t.7.25.2: Then there was a great grove of Laṅkā named Nikumbhilā; the great-souled lord of the Rākṣasas entered it together with his followers.
t.7.25.3: There he saw a sacrifice in progress, strewn with hundreds of sacrificial posts and adorned with gracious shrines, blazing, as it were, with splendor.
t.7.25.4: Then he saw there his own son Meghanāda, the subduer of foes, wearing a black antelope skin, with a water pot and a tuft of hair as his emblems.
t.7.25.6: Then Uśanas, the preceptor, the best of the twice-born, of great austerity, spoke there to Rāvaṇa, the best of the Rākṣasas, for the success of the sacrifice.
t.7.25.5: The lord of the Rākṣasas approached him, embraced him with his arms, and said: "What is this that is going on, my child? Tell me that."
t.7.25.7: I shall tell you, O king; let it all be heard. Those seven sacrifices, very grand in their extent, have been accomplished by your son.
t.7.25.8: The Agniṣṭoma and the Aśvamedha, the sacrifice Bahusuvarṇaka, likewise the sacrifice Rājasūya, the Gomedha, and likewise the Vaiṣṇava.
t.7.25.9: When the Māheśvara sacrifice, so very hard for men to attain, was undertaken, your son received boons here from Paśupati himself, face to face.
t.7.25.10: A divine chariot that goes wherever one wishes and surely travels through the sky, and the illusion called Tāmasī, by which darkness is brought about.
t.7.25.11: Indeed, O lord of the Rākṣasas, by means of this māyā the movements of one fighting in battle cannot be known by the Suras and Asuras.
t.7.25.12: Two quivers inexhaustible in arrows, a bow that is very hard to overcome, and also, O gentle one, a mighty weapon that destroys enemies in battle.
t.7.25.14: Then Daśagrīva said, "This has not been done well, since enemies led by Indra have been honored with offerings."
t.7.25.13: Having obtained all these boons, O Daśānana, I, this son of yours, stand here today at the completion of the sacrifice, awaiting you.
t.7.25.16: Then Daśagrīva, having gone there together with his son and with Vibhīṣaṇa, caused all those women, overcome with tears, to descend.
t.7.25.15: Come now, for what has been done cannot be undone. Come, gentle one, let us go back to our own home.
t.7.25.18: But Vibhīṣaṇa, righteous of soul, seeing those women overwhelmed with grief and knowing his intent, spoke these words.
t.7.25.17: Bearing auspicious marks, they were the very jewels among the gods, Dānavas and Rākṣasas, adorned with ornaments of many kinds and blazing with their own splendour.
t.7.25.19: With such conduct as this, which destroys fame, wealth and family, you inflict violence upon living beings and act according to your own will.
t.7.25.20: These beautiful women were carried off by you after you had assaulted their kinsmen; and now, O king, Kumbhīnasī has been abducted by Madhu, who has overridden you.
t.7.25.21: But Rāvaṇa spoke these words: "I do not understand what this is. And who is this one whom you have spoken of, called Madhu by name?"
t.7.25.22: But Vibhīṣaṇa, greatly enraged, spoke these words to his brother: "Hear now the fruit that has come of this sinful deed."
t.7.25.23: The elder brother of our maternal grandfather Sumālin, the night-ranger renowned as Mālyavān, old and wise…
t.7.25.24: The eldest brother of our mother's father was our venerable grandsire, and Kumbhīnasī was the daughter of his daughter.
t.7.25.25: Now that maiden, born of Analā, our mother's sister, is indeed by dharma the sister of us brothers.
t.7.25.26: She was carried off, O king, by Madhu, a rākṣasa of great might, while your son was engaged in the sacrifice and I was dwelling within the waters.
t.7.25.27: Having slain the foremost of the rākṣasas, your esteemed ministers, and having overpowered them, he carried her off, O king, though she was guarded within your inner apartments.
t.7.25.28: Having heard this, great king, it was pardoned and he was not slain, for a maiden must surely be given to a husband by those who give her away. This has come to pass in this very world; let it be known to you.
t.7.25.29: Then Daśagrīva, enraged, his eyes reddened with fury, said: "Let my chariot be made ready at once, and let the heroes prepare themselves for battle!"
t.7.25.30: Let my brother Kumbhakarṇa and those who are the foremost of the night-rangers mount their vehicles, bearing weapons and arms of various kinds.
t.7.25.31: Today, having slain in battle that Madhu who has no fear of Rāvaṇa, I shall go to the world of Indra, eager for war and surrounded by my friends.
t.7.25.32: Then, having conquered heaven and brought Puraṃdara under my control, I shall roam about at ease, adorned with sovereignty over the three worlds.
t.7.25.33: Four thousand fierce akṣauhiṇīs of rākṣasas eager for battle, armed with weapons of many kinds, swiftly marched forth.
t.7.25.34: Indrajit, taking charge of the army and its soldiers, went at the front; the valiant Rāvaṇa was in the middle, and Kumbhakarṇa at the rear.
t.7.25.35: Vibhīṣaṇa, righteous of soul, practised dharma in Laṅkā, while all those highly fortunate ones went toward the city of Madhu.
t.7.25.36: On chariots, elephants, donkeys, camels, blazing horses and great serpents, all the Rākṣasas set forth, filling the sky without a gap.
t.7.25.37: And there the Daityas by the hundreds, who had made enmity with the gods, seeing Rāvaṇa going forth, followed behind him.
t.7.25.38: But Daśānana, having gone to Madhupura and entered it, did not see Madhu there; there he saw only his sister.
t.7.25.39: Then Kumbhīnasī, the sister of that king of the Rākṣasas, terrified, bowed low with joined palms and fell with her head at his feet.
t.7.25.40: Rāvaṇa, foremost of the Rākṣasas, raised her up, saying, "Do not be afraid; what can I do for you?"
t.7.25.41: She said, "If you are pleased with me, O king, O mighty one, then you should not kill my husband here today, O bestower of honour."
t.7.25.42: Be true to your word, O lord of kings, and look upon me as I beg you. For you yourself said, O mighty-armed one, 'There is nothing to fear.'
t.7.25.43: But Rāvaṇa, emboldened, said to his sister who stood there: "And where is this husband of yours? Let it be told to me quickly."
t.7.25.44: Together with him I shall go to the world of the gods for conquest. Out of compassion and affection for you, I have refrained from slaying Madhu.
t.7.25.45: Thus addressed, the rākṣasī roused that very wise night-roamer, who lay fast asleep, and, as if overjoyed, spoke to him.
t.7.25.46: Here has arrived Daśagrīva, my brother, the night-roamer, who longs to conquer the world of the gods, and he chooses you as his ally in this help.
t.7.25.47: Therefore, O Rākṣasa, go together with your kinsmen to lend him your aid; it is fitting to work for the cause of one who is affectionate and devoted to you.
t.7.25.48: Hearing her words, Madhu spoke the words "So be it," and approaching in the proper manner, he saw the foremost of the Rākṣasas.
t.7.25.49: He duly honored Rāvaṇa, lord of the Rākṣasas, as dharma required. Having received that honor, the mighty Daśagrīva spent one night there in Madhu's dwelling and then prepared to depart.
t.7.25.50: Then, having reached Mount Kailāsa, the abode of Vaiśravaṇa, the lord of the Rākṣasas, resembling the great Indra, encamped his army.
